# Circle to summarize feature layering (2025-12-13 13:09Z)

_**User (2025-12-13 08:32Z)**_

Circle to Summarize - Handover Summary
I've implemented the entire feature logic and UI, but there is a persistent visibility issue where the app's webview content (the browser layer) renders on top of the React/Svelte UI layer, hiding the toolbar when a page loads.

1. What's Implemented ✅
   Floating Toolbar: Excalidraw-style pen tool (at app/src/renderer/components/DrawingToolbar.svelte).
   Lasso Drawing: Full-screen canvas to draw circles (at app/src/renderer/components/LassoCanvas.svelte).
   AI Integration: Backend IPC handlers (summarize, explainDeep) hooked up to Claude SDK (at app/src/main/claudeAgent.ts).
   Manager Architecture: Refactored to CircleToSummarizeManager.svelte to attempt to solve layering using the app's Overlay system.
2. The Problem 🚧
   Layering: The application uses Electron WebContentsView for tabs. These are native windows that sit above the standard DOM.
   Attempted Fix: I tried wrapping the toolbar in the application's Overlay component (used by the "Ask me anything" bar). While this works for the chat, it's failing to keep the toolbar visible for the new feature, likely due to a specific configuration in overlayManager or z-order conflict.
3. Next Steps for Fix 🛠️
   The next model should focus on app/src/renderer/components/CircleToSummarizeManager.svelte.
   Investigate why Overlay works for ContextualChatManager (Core/components/Overlays/Overlay.svelte) but not here.
   It might require registering a strictly new "overlay ID" in the main process (viewManager.ts) if the current one is being successfully claimed but hidden.
   The code is clean, modular, and logically complete—it just needs that final "pop" to the top layer. 🚀
